proof:
Source: steps 2c–2d of the supplied proof of the parent node root.stationary_results-a1.divergence_identity-a1 (extension by zero of the chart field w̃, and vanishing of ∫ trace Dw̄ for w̄ ∈ C¹_c), here stated for an arbitrary field.

Notation:
- ℝⁿ := EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n) = Rn n, and Lⁿ := volume.
- Dw(x) := fderiv ℝ w x, and trace := LinearMap.trace ℝ (Rn n).
- e_1, …, e_n := EuclideanSpace.basisFun (Fin n) ℝ, an orthonormal basis with ⟨e_j, v⟩ = v_j.
- π_j := EuclideanSpace.proj j, the continuous linear map v ↦ v_j.

1. (Preliminaries.) Q is compact in the Hausdorff space ℝⁿ, hence closed, so Qᶜ is open. V is open, hence measurable. Since w is C¹ on the open set V, for every x ∈ V the map w is C¹ at x (ContDiffOn.contDiffAt, as V ∈ 𝓝 x), and in particular differentiable at x.

2. (Extension by zero.) Define w̄ : ℝⁿ → ℝⁿ by w̄(x) := w(x) for x ∈ V and w̄(x) := 0 for x ∉ V.
 (a) If x ∈ V, then w̄ = w on the open neighbourhood V of x, i.e. w̄ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] w.
 (b) If x ∉ Q, then w̄ = 0 on the open neighbourhood Qᶜ of x. Indeed, for z ∈ Qᶜ either z ∈ V, and then w̄(z) = w(z) = 0 by hypothesis since z ∈ V ∖ Q; or z ∉ V, and then w̄(z) = 0 by definition. In particular w̄(x) = 0 for every x ∉ Q.

3. (w̄ is C¹ on ℝⁿ.) Because Q ⊆ V, every x ∈ ℝⁿ lies in V or in Qᶜ.
 - If x ∈ V, w is C¹ at x (step 1) and w̄ =ᶠ[𝓝 x] w (2a), so w̄ is C¹ at x (ContDiffAt.congr_of_eventuallyEq).
 - If x ∉ Q, w̄ agrees near x with the constant 0 (2b), which is C¹.
 Hence ContDiffAt ℝ 1 w̄ x for every x, i.e. ContDiff ℝ 1 w̄ (contDiff_iff_contDiffAt).

4. (Compact support.) By 2b, support w̄ ⊆ Q. Since Q is compact, w̄ has compact support (HasCompactSupport.intro).

5. (Derivatives.) For x ∈ V, Dw̄(x) = Dw(x), by 2a and Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq. For x ∉ Q, Dw̄(x) = 0, by 2b and Filter.EventuallyEq.fderiv_eq.

6. (Passing to ℝⁿ.)
 - By step 5 on the measurable set V (setIntegral_congr_fun), ∫_V trace Dw(x) dx = ∫_V trace Dw̄(x) dx.
 - If x ∉ V then x ∉ Q (as Q ⊆ V), so Dw̄(x) = 0 and trace Dw̄(x) = 0. Hence ∫_V trace Dw̄ = ∫_{ℝⁿ} trace Dw̄ (setIntegral_eq_integral_of_forall_compl_eq_zero).
 Thus ∫_V trace Dw = ∫_{ℝⁿ} trace Dw̄.

7. (Coordinates.) For j = 1, …, n put w̄_j := π_j ∘ w̄, i.e. w̄_j(x) = w̄(x)_j = ⟨e_j, w̄(x)⟩.
 - Since π_j is continuous linear, w̄_j : ℝⁿ → ℝ is C¹ (ContinuousLinearMap.contDiff composed with step 3).
 - w̄_j has compact support (HasCompactSupport.comp_left, using π_j(0) = 0).
 - By the chain rule, Dw̄_j(x) = π_j ∘ Dw̄(x). Hence Dw̄_j(x) e_j = (Dw̄(x) e_j)_j = ⟨e_j, Dw̄(x) e_j⟩ (EuclideanSpace.basisFun_inner).

8. (Trace as a sum.) For every linear map L of ℝⁿ and the orthonormal basis (e_j), trace L = Σ_j ⟨e_j, L e_j⟩ (LinearMap.trace_eq_sum_inner). With step 7, trace Dw̄(x) = Σ_j Dw̄_j(x) e_j for every x ∈ ℝⁿ.

9. (Integrability and splitting the integral.) For each j, the function x ↦ Dw̄_j(x) e_j:
 - is continuous, because Dw̄_j is continuous when w̄_j is C¹ (ContDiff.continuous_fderiv, then apply to the constant vector e_j);
 - has compact support, because it vanishes outside tsupport w̄_j (HasCompactSupport.fderiv_apply);
 - is therefore integrable on ℝⁿ (Continuous.integrable_of_hasCompactSupport).
 By step 8 and additivity of the integral over a finite sum (integral_finsetSum), ∫_{ℝⁿ} trace Dw̄ = Σ_j ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dw̄_j(x) e_j dx.

10. (Lemma: the integral of a directional derivative of a C¹_c function vanishes.) Let g : ℝⁿ → ℝ be C¹ with compact support and v ∈ ℝⁿ. Then ∫_{ℝⁿ} Dg(x) v dx = 0.
 Proof. Apply the integration-by-parts formula integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable (Mathlib module Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts) with the measure volume, which is an additive Haar measure on ℝⁿ, and with f :≡ 1 the constant function, g and v. Its hypotheses hold:
 - x ↦ Df(x)v · g(x) is the zero function (Df ≡ 0), hence integrable;
 - x ↦ f(x) · Dg(x)v = Dg(x)v is continuous with compact support, as in step 9, hence integrable;
 - x ↦ f(x) g(x) = g(x) is continuous with compact support, hence integrable;
 - f is differentiable everywhere (constant), and g is differentiable everywhere (C¹).
 The formula gives ∫ 1 · Dg(x)v dx = −∫ Df(x)v · g(x) dx = −∫ 0 dx = 0. (Equivalently: Fubini and the fundamental theorem of calculus on lines parallel to v.)

11. (Conclusion.) Apply step 10 with g := w̄_j, which is C¹ with compact support by step 7, and v := e_j. This gives ∫ Dw̄_j(x) e_j dx = 0 for each j. By steps 6 and 9, ∫_V trace Dw(x) dx = ∫_{ℝⁿ} trace Dw̄ = Σ_j 0 = 0. ∎

Implementation note: integral_mul_fderiv_eq_neg_fderiv_mul_of_integrable is not imported by GMT.Ch02.Submission. Add `import Mathlib.Analysis.Calculus.LineDeriv.IntegrationByParts`. It was checked that adding it leaves the fully elaborated (pp.all) terms of all frozen contract definitions byte-identical.
key_steps: Extend w by 0 off V. Since Q ⊆ V is compact and w = 0 on V ∖ Q, the extension w̄ is C¹ on ℝⁿ with support in Q, Dw̄ = Dw on V and Dw̄ = 0 off Q.
∫_V trace Dw = ∫_{ℝⁿ} trace Dw̄, by congruence on V and because the integrand vanishes off V ⊇ Q.
trace Dw̄(x) = Σ_j D(w̄_j)(x) e_j with w̄_j = ⟨e_j, w̄⟩ ∈ C¹_c (trace_eq_sum_inner and the chain rule). Each term is continuous with compact support, so the integral splits into a finite sum.
∫ Dg(x) v dx = 0 for every g ∈ C¹_c(ℝⁿ), by integration by parts against the constant function 1. Summing over j gives 0.
